submission.natural_language_explanation: L1/H2 is a dense local-value head: at each measured position its attention lands on one nearby token — nearly always the token just before it, sometimes the position itself, otherwise the text's first token — and it writes one fixed linear image of that token's layer-0 value into the residual stream, so its strength above the 0.83 floor is just how far that single attended token's value sits from the head's mean write. It crosses 0.25x max where the token it lands on is a high-value one: existential 'there' before a verb anywhere in the text ('there is/are/was/were/will be/has been/goes', including mid-sentence in 'The report says there is a problem'), 'here'/'where' before a verb ('here is/are', 'where is/are/did'), a locative 'there' after a verb in a short text that does not open with 'The' ('He ran there', 'She lives there now'; 8 of 10 measured), the second piece of a rare split word or a non-Latin byte ('Mc|Av|oy', 'Mac|mill|an', 'Sch|ir|mer', 'McL|ach|lan', bark|ed, cheer|ed, сп|ос, Thai/Japanese/Cyrillic pieces), a numeral ('3.50', 'Line 12', '42 years'), or one of a short mid set — 'all' before a noun ('all day', 'all week', 'all the way'), 'up'/'down' after a verb, 'last' before a noun, and 'not' after do/did/does/could/can. It stays at 0.00-0.20x max wherever every position's sharpest attention falls only on 'the'/'The', ',', '.', 'is'/'was'/'are', 'in'/'to'/'at'/'for'/'with' or the text's first token, which is the standard state of one-word texts (0 of 10 measured) and of short (2-8 token) 'The'-opened declaratives with no prepositional phrase, split piece, numeral, 'there/here/where' or mid-set word (0 of 39 measured, median 0.03x max); ordinary prose of 10+ tokens straddles the line (median peak exactly at 0.25x max, 15 of 30 sentences active) and a verb followed by 'on the' also sits on it (7 of 20 active), so neither of those is a reliable negative.

rival_explanations: The head is a low-frequency/rarity detector: all its strong cases are rare tokens, so it should fire after any uncommon word (a technical noun or a foreign name) and stay quiet on the frequent words 'there', 'here', 'all' and 'and' and after auxiliary+'not', which my hypothesis calls strong.

The head is a non-ASCII/encoding detector: its scan's strongest examples are all mojibake and byte fragments, so it should fire on any non-Latin-script or byte text and stay quiet on every pure-ASCII English text, existential 'there is' included.

The head is a broad previous-token head with no per-token preference: it fires wherever attention lands on the preceding token at 0.6 or more, so almost every fluent English text of six or more tokens should be active, short 'The'-opened declaratives and one-word-plus-period texts included.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The protein sample seems stable enough.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Another uncommon technical noun tokenized whole in a plain 7-token 'The'-opened declarative, separating token rarity from the hypothesis's named triggers.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The enzyme mixture looks stable today.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Rare-but-whole vocabulary ('enzyme', 'mixture', 'stable') with no split piece, where rarity and the claimed feature come apart in the reliable negative class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The engine noise grows louder lately.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The guests all leave early tomorrow.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The battery will surely last forever.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The children, not adults, left.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Puts the token ' not' after a comma instead of after do/did/does/could/can, the only context the hypothesis calls high-value for ' not'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The up train leaves early today.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Puts the token ' up' before a noun rather than after a verb, so the hypothesis's 'up/down after a verb' condition is not met.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The trail ends here anyway.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Puts the token ' here' before an adverb rather than a verb, testing whether ' here' is high-value only in the 'here is/are' frame the hypothesis names.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The flight takes many tedious hours.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A spelled-out quantity rather than a numeral token, so the hypothesis's numeral condition is absent while the topic still reads as counting.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The engine is cold this morning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The inspectors believe there are serious faults.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The auditors found there have been errors.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The warden said here are your keys.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The tourists ask where is the museum.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We go there every summer.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The crew works all night long.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' all' immediately before the noun 'night', the hypothesis's mid-set 'all before a noun' case, though the rarity rival calls ' all' a frequent word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee could not agree.
adversarial_test_results.detail: ' not' after the modal 'could', the auxiliary+'not' case the hypothesis calls high-value and the rarity rival calls quiet.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The editor reads line 12 daily.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A single numeral token (' 12') followed by another token, testing the numeral class beyond the claimed example '3.50'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: В отчёте ошибка.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Short Cyrillic text that tokenizes into non-Latin byte pieces with none of the claimed ASCII tokens, the hypothesis's non-Latin case in another language at the negatives' length.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Λάθος μένει.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Short Greek text, a non-Latin script absent from the scan examples, predicted active by the hypothesis's non-Latin byte clause.
